- monitor `built` was re-armed with the call that declared it (`monitor {"name":"built","path":"out.txt","ttl_ms":600000}`); its TTL starts again from now.
- job `j9` (slug `build`, had run 1m35s when the daemon stopped): NOT run again — its process was the old daemon's, and a crash may have left it running (check with `pkill` pattern="<a fragment of its command>" action="list", which kills nothing). Its output went to `build.log`, which survives — read that. To run it again: `bash {"command":"cargo build > build.log 2>&1","background":true,"cwd":"/w","slug":"build"}`.
  Rows that waited on it: `ship once the build is done`. Their wait is RELEASED — a job this daemon never ran reads as ended, so they are no longer blocked on it; if they still need its result, run it again and set `wait_on` on the row to the new handle with `todo_write`.
Nothing above is running now. Bring back only what still matters: `task_resume` for a subagent, `monitor` for a watch, `bash` for a job.
